ground_truth.description: Factory.deploy uses create2 but reverts with CreateCollision if address exists, violating ERC-4337 expectation to return address. Breaks simulations and bundler logic.
ground_truth.root_cause: Factory.deploy uses create2 but reverts with CreateCollision if address exists, violating ERC-4337 expectation to return address. Breaks simulations and bundler logic.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: Deploy wallet once, call deploy again → reverts. Attacker can front-run to cause DoS. PoC: test_factory_double_deploy_PoC in AuditPoC.sol. Shows first deploy succeeds, second reverts.
ground_truth.fix_description: Check if address exists via predicted.code.length, return it if so.

vulnerabilities.explanation: deploy() performs CREATE2 and unconditionally reverts with DeployFailed when the resulting address is zero (which occurs on CREATE2 collision). No check for pre-existing code at the predicted address is performed, violating the ERC-4337 expectation that deploy returns the existing address instead of reverting.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. Attacker observes a pending deploy(_mainModule, _salt) tx. 2. Attacker front-runs with identical parameters, causing the first deployment to succeed. 3. Victim's tx now hits the collision path and reverts. 4. Repeated front-running prevents any subsequent deploy calls for that salt, breaking wallet creation and bundler simulations.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Before CREATE2, compute the predicted address with keccak256(0xff || address(this) || _salt || keccak256(code)). If that address already has code (extcodesize > 0), return it directly; otherwise proceed with CREATE2.

prediction.overall_explanation: The deploy function reverts on address collision instead of returning the existing address, enabling trivial front-running DOS against wallet deployments and breaking ERC-4337 simulation expectations.
